pride_data.title: The dynamic configuration and phosphorylation of the C-terminal HEAT domain of huntingtin modulates its function
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study different forms of human huntingtin (HTT). The variants included wild-type protein with poly-Q tail lengths of 23 and 78 and Ser2116 > Ala mutation of Q23- and Q78-HTT. Cross-linking was performed using the homobifunctional, lysine-reactive disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS).
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014; Vijayvargia et al., eLife, 2016). Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin and digests were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography. SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Elite instrument. Additional details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequence of the target protein.  Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance -5 to +5 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; huntingtin
